instruction: GUI-only requirement: Complete the task entirely in the KiCad graphical user interface (Project Manager, Schematic Editor, and PCB Editor). Do not open Command Prompt, PowerShell, Terminal, or any shell; do not run kicad-cli, pcbnew in batch mode, Python, or other helper scripts/code that directly generates or edits the deliverable files. Use only KiCad native GUI tools, menus, dialogs, and built-in save/export commands. Clock Trace Topology: Star to Daisy Chain The file board.kicad_pcb has a 100 MHz clock (net CLK) routed as a star topology: one source (U1) fans out to three loads (U2, U3, U4) through a common hub. A series-termination resistor footprint (R_TERM, 22R) sits in a scratch area with no net connection. Re-route CLK as a daisy chain with R_TERM inserted as a series terminator between the source and the first load. Split the net into CLK_PRE (source side) and CLK (load side). Move R_TERM to a position between U1 and the load chain. Requirements: 1. Net CLK_PRE exists; U1 output pad is on CLK_PRE. 2. Net CLK exists; U2, U3, U4 input pads are on CLK. 3. R_TERM pad "1" is on CLK_PRE; R_TERM pad "2" is on CLK. 4. CLK net topology is a chain (no node with 3+ segments meeting - no star junction). 5. Total CLK segment length <= 100 mm. Write /home/user/Desktop/answer.kicad_pcb.
